central_topic: Post-draft citation repair for an empirical study that predicts the expected cover time of simple random walks on small connected graphs (5 <= n <= 30) from cheap graph statistics and compares the predictor with classical cover-time bounds. Two gaps are in scope: (1) comparator provenance, since the Matthews-type reference has no citation and the (4/27)n^3 upper bound is cited to Feige's lower-bound paper; (2) the family-specific cover-time asymptotics named in Background > Positioning and relied on in the Discussion.
core_methods: Matthews method: cover time <= max hitting time x H_{n-1}, the bound behind the Matthews-type reference (Background 'Graph-aware characterizations', Method 'Compared predictors', Table 2)
comparators: Feige tight upper bound (4/27)n^3 + o(n^3), the cubic term of the primary best-bound comparator (currently misattributed to Feige1995ATL, the lower-bound paper)
Matthews hitting-time cover-time bound (Table 2 row, error 0.605; currently uncited)
benchmarks: cover-time asymptotics for evaluated test families: random 3-regular graphs, Erdos-Renyi graphs above the connectivity threshold, 2D grids/tori (Positioning paragraph and Discussion)
result_driven_themes: near-n ln n regime of random regular and dense Erdos-Renyi graphs, where gains over the bounds are largest (Discussion)
grid cover time is not a single power law at this scale (n log^2 n asymptotics), offered as the reason grids have high residual error (Discussion)

queries.query: Feige A tight upper bound on the cover time for random walks on graphs
queries.rationale: Gap target related-work-comparators (high). The (4/27)n^3 term of the primary best-bound comparator is cited to Feige1995ATL ('A Tight Lower Bound...') in the Introduction, Background, Design rationale and Discussion (lollipop attains (4/27)n^3). The separate upper-bound paper is needed to fix the attribution. The first-pass query for it hit HTTP 429, so this uses the exact title to avoid matching the lower-bound paper already in the bib.

queries.query: Matthews Covering problems for Markov chains Annals of Probability
queries.rationale: Gap target related-work-comparators (high). The Matthews-type reference (max hitting time x H_{n-1}) is a Table 2 comparator, described as 'a more demanding comparison' and listed under Compared predictors, but it has no citation. The first-pass query returned zero candidates, so this uses the exact title plus venue.

queries.query: Levin Peres Wilmer Markov Chains and Mixing Times cover time Matthews method
queries.rationale: Optional textbook anchor from the gap memo for the Matthews method and for computing hitting times by linear solve (Method, Matthews-type reference). This is also a fallback if the 1988 Matthews article is not indexed. Add at most one textbook citation.

queries.query: Cooper Frieze The cover time of random regular graphs
queries.rationale: Gap target positioning-family-asymptotics (medium). The Positioning sentence 'asymptotics for specific families' has no citation, and the Discussion places random 3-regular graphs in the near-n ln n regime where gains are largest. The asymptotic for random r-regular graphs ((r-1)/(r-2) n ln n) grounds both.

queries.query: Cooper Frieze The cover time of sparse random graphs
queries.rationale: Gap target positioning-family-asymptotics (medium). The Discussion says Erdos-Renyi graphs, sampled from p ~ 2 ln n / n up to 0.5, sit near the n ln n regime and move between sparse and dense behaviour. The G(n, c ln n / n) cover-time asymptotic covers exactly this density range.

queries.query: Dembo Peres Rosen Zeitouni Cover times for Brownian motion and random walks in two dimensions
queries.rationale: Gap target positioning-family-asymptotics (medium). The Discussion suggests that grid cover time is not a single power law in the statistics at this scale, as the explanation for high grid error. The 2D torus asymptotic (4/pi) n log^2 n grounds this. It also covers the remaining family named in the Positioning gap.
